title: Shadow Open Market Committee: Further Firming Necessary, and Soon
summary: Two days after the FOMC held (10-2), Musalem says 'additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon,' arguing policy and financial conditions remain accommodative and that earlier, smaller steps while expectations are anchored beat larger, abrupt moves later. He pointedly downplays the recent tightening of financial conditions ('not overly concerned'), which cuts against the Chair's reading that policy is working through financial conditions, and he sees demand (AI capex, wealth effects, fiscal, deregulation) keeping growth at or above potential while broad-based inflation runs at 3% or more with risks skewed up. Versus his September 21 Reuters interview the core message is unchanged (accommodative policy, earlier and incremental firming, an 18-month horizon), but it is now formalized in the two-scenario framework from his LSE lecture and adds an explicit, less-likely scenario in which no further firming is needed (lower energy and shipping costs, productivity, or a demand slowdown). Labor is a non-issue for policy: stable near full employment, symmetric risks and 'not driving inflation,' with only long-term unemployment flagged as worth watching; he is a 2026 non-voter.

key_quotes.quote: I judge that additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon.
key_quotes.context: Fourth of his four headline messages, delivered two days after the October hold.

key_quotes.quote: I believe that monetary policy and financial conditions remain accommodative.
key_quotes.context: His read of the stance even after the September hike and the recent widening of credit spreads.

key_quotes.quote: The economy remained solid after those events, so I am not overly concerned by the recent tightening of financial conditions.
key_quotes.context: Compares the recent FCI tightening with Liberation Day and the start of the Middle East conflict; rejects it as a substitute for firming.

key_quotes.quote: Nonetheless, inflation is elevated and broad-based, and I perceive meaningful risk that above-target inflation will persist longer than consistent with price stability.
key_quotes.context: Inflation section, right after saying the labor market is not driving inflation.
